text: An old potter had one bowl he loved above the rest
One rainy morning his apprentice carried it across
He slipped on a wet stone, and the bowl was lost
Forgive me, master, I will throw the pieces away
But the old man knelt and gathered every piece that day
Day after day he joined them, with lacquer and with gold
Why mend it, asked the boy, it will never be the same
No, said the potter, it will be more beautiful
And he poured from it for every dearest guest who came
Your cracks are not your end, mend them in gold
